text:
incident-bot: PAGED: Streaming SLO breach detected (p99) in us-west-2 for model redwood-open-1. Alert: cont-batching path high tail latency.

pagerduty: Pager duty triggered for eng-sre. Priority: P1.

Jen (oncall): I'm on it. seeing customer-facing latency spike on streaming routes. p95 ~ 600ms, p99 ~ 2.9s.

Sam (runtime): rolling deploy 1769996 went out ~12:10UTC. included batcher heuristic change: increased default max_batch_size and switched to sequence-length weighting.

Mira (sre): svc metrics show streaming stalls (stream open -> first token delay) increased. KV cache evictions spiked at same time. cpu on packer nodes high for a subset of tenants.

CS - Priya: two customers reported interactive lag and slow replies, not errors. they see >2s delays, affecting UI.

Jen (oncall): ok timeline lines up with deploy. can we toggle the new heuristic off and cap batch size for streaming routes? we need a mitigation that preserves throughput.

Sam (runtime): on it. flipping feature flag: `batcher.seq_weighting = off` and set `max_batch_size.streaming = 128` for us-west-2. applying via config-service now.

deploy-bot: feature-flag update applied: batcher.seq_weighting -> off (env: us-west-2).

Sam (runtime): also adding `pack_timeout_ms` cut from 30 -> 12 for streaming to favor latency. Pushing change to packer nodes.

Mira (sre): after the flag flip, p95 dropped to ~280ms within two minutes, p99 trending down to 1.1s. KV evictions also decreasing.

Alex (prod-eng): good short-term. we should consider adding fair-share allocations by sequence-length buckets rather than pure weight, to avoid long sequences starving short interactive streams.

Jen (oncall): agree. for this incident: mitigation = feature-flag rollback of seq weighting + streaming batch cap + lower pack timeout. Customer impact: degraded UX only, no errors; CS notified.

CS - Priya: forwarded mitigation notes to affected customers, they acknowledged improvement.

Sam (runtime): quick note: config diff that triggered this had `max_batch_size = 1024` and `seq_weight_factor = 3` on the default policy. that combination caused large mixed-length packs and KV churn.

Mira (sre): action items: 1) revert heuristic in canary and add gate 2) add alert for KV eviction rate correlated with p99 3) add a streaming-specific SLO threshold and guardrail to cap batching for low-latency routes 4) postmortem.

Alex (prod-eng): also recommend a test harness load that mixes very long and very short sequences to reproduce packer starvation. we should simulate multi-tenant sequences.

Jen (oncall): creating incident ticket and assigning owners. timeline: 12:10 deploy -> 12:13 alerts -> 12:17 flag flip -> 12:19 p99 improved -> 12:25 stable. Marking primary mitigations as successful.

Sam (runtime): I will open PR to add per-route batch caps and a gradual rollout strategy for seq weighting with safety checks.

Mira (sre): I'll add an automated check that flags high KV churn + packer CPU > 75% as a paging condition.

Jen (oncall): nic e work. we'll hold for 30 mins to watch, then start the postmortem. closing pager if stable. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident moved to INVESTIGATING -> MITIGATED (updated by Jen).
